item.bailer.desc: A scoop with a handle, cut from a plastic jerrycan. The most useful thing in a boat after a capsize.
item.bailer.name: Bailer
item.bottle_letter.desc: A green bottle, crusted with barnacles and sealed with wax. Inside, a sheet of squared paper rolled into a tube.
item.bottle_letter.name: Message in a bottle
item.brass_screws.desc: A paper twist of brass screws. Brass doesn't rust in sea water, which is why boats get it.
item.brass_screws.name: Brass screws
item.knot_cord.desc: A metre of braided cord with melted ends. Keep it in your pocket and tie bowlines until your hands do it by themselves.
item.knot_cord.name: Knot cord
item.life_jacket.desc: Orange, three buckles, the boathouse's number on the back. They won't let you afloat without it — and quite right too.
item.life_jacket.name: Life jacket
item.lucky_whistle.desc: A yellow plastic whistle on a string, chewed at one corner. Somebody very small believes in it very much.
item.lucky_whistle.name: Lucky whistle
item.race_mark.desc: An orange inflatable buoy with a “3” on it, gone limp, all sand and weed. The storm took it; without it the school can't lay its triangle.
item.race_mark.name: Race mark (deflated)
item.sail_book.desc: A pocket book in an oilcloth cover: points of sail, knots, right of way and what to do when the boat lies down. With drawings in the margins.
item.sail_book.name: “The Young Helmsman's School”
item.sail_card.desc: A little blue book with a golden ray on the cover. Its pages take the stamps for lessons, ranks and races. Smells of varnish and, faintly, of the sea.
item.sail_card.name: Luch membership book
item.sail_gloves.desc: Leather palms, cut-off fingers. The sheet doesn't burn your hands in them when a gust tries to tear it from your fist.
item.sail_gloves.name: Sailing gloves
item.sail_pennant.desc: A triangular pennant: a white field, a golden ray out of the corner. They're given for a season lived on the water.
item.sail_pennant.name: Luch school pennant
item.yacht_varnish.desc: A tin of varnish the colour of buckwheat honey. Three coats and the wood will outlast any of us.
item.yacht_varnish.name: Yacht varnish

sail.board.results.title: RESULTS
sail.hire.closed: No hire just now. Have a look at the mast: it explains better than I do.
sail.hire.done: Number nine, {0} roubles. Be back an hour before sunset and bring her back in one piece.
sail.hire.left_elsewhere: First bring back the one you left. Boats don't walk home.
sail.hire.no_cert: No helmsman's certificate, no boat on your own. It's not spite — I'm the one who has to mend her afterwards.
sail.hire.no_certificate: No helmsman's certificate, no boat on your own. No offence: I've one boat, and your mother has one of you.
sail.hire.no_money: Hire is {0} roubles. Short? Then sit on the slip, that's free.
sail.hire.ok: Number nine is yours. Be back an hour before sunset and hose her down.
sail.hire.returned: Got her. Give her a hose-down — salt does a boat no favours.
sail.hire.taken: Number nine's out with a group just now. Wait till they're back and she's yours.
sail.hire.towed: Your boat came home on a tow: she's on the slip. You owe a fine and your word of honour.
sail.jacket.need: No going afloat without a life jacket. The rail is in the changing room.
sail.jacket.returned: Hung the jacket back in its place, buckles out, so it dries.
sail.jacket.taken: Found a jacket my size, did up the three buckles, tugged at the shoulders: it sits.
sail.join.already: You're one of ours already — there's your name in the register. Off to the boats with you.
sail.join.done: You're on the roll. Here's your card: don't lose it and don't soak it. The first lesson is ashore, with any coach.
sail.join.no_money: The fee's {0} roubles. Short? Never mind, the sea will wait. Come back when you've saved up — the knots you can practise for free meanwhile.
sail.join.offer: Want to join? We take anyone who isn't afraid of getting wet. The season's fee is {0} roubles, and the membership book comes free.
sail.join.ok: A new name on the roll: yours. The blue sailor's card is in your pocket and the fee is paid. The first lesson is ashore.
sail.lesson.capsize.done: Twice over and twice up. Now you know the main thing: a capsize is wet, not frightening.
sail.lesson.capsize.fail: Enough swimming, let's get you warm. We'll finish when the water's in a kinder mood.
sail.lesson.capsize.hint1: Onto the centreboard! Feet right at its tip, hands on the gunwale — and lean back with all your weight. Don't rush her, she's thinking.
sail.lesson.capsize.intro: Today we go over on purpose. It's not an accident, it's an exercise, like a forward roll in the gym. When she's down, don't let go of her: swim round to the centreboard, stand on it and pull on the gunwale. She'll come up. I'm right here in the launch.
sail.lesson.capsize.obj1: Capsize and right the boat: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.capsize.title: Capsize: over and up again
sail.lesson.first_sail.done: And that's it: you sailed her yourself. Remember how the boat began to chuckle on the water — that was her saying hello.
sail.lesson.first_sail.fail: Back to the slip. You've seen plenty for a first time; the rest next time out.
sail.lesson.first_sail.hint1: Closer to me! Push the tiller away and the bow comes towards you. Gently, like closing a door.
sail.lesson.first_sail.hint2: The wind should be square on your side. If the sail's flapping, sheet in until it goes quiet.
sail.lesson.first_sail.intro: Today you just follow my launch. Sheet in one hand, tiller in the other. If she heels, ease the sheet and she'll stand up by herself. That's all you need to know for now.
sail.lesson.first_sail.obj1: Follow the coach's launch: {0} of {1} s
sail.lesson.first_sail.obj2: Hold a beam reach: {0} of {1} s
sail.lesson.first_sail.title: First sail
sail.lesson.gate.cold_water: The water is too cold for this lesson. We'll do our capsizing when it warms up.
sail.lesson.gate.done_before: That lesson is already in your card. Want it again? Go on, the sea won't run short.
sail.lesson.gate.hours: Not enough hours afloat. The sea teaches faster than the blackboard: put in some more and come back.
sail.lesson.gate.not_member: Join the school first: the roll is on the coach's desk.
sail.lesson.gate.order: Not so fast: the lesson before this one comes first. We teach in order here.
sail.lesson.gate.race: Sail at least one race first. Without it this lesson is only words.
sail.lesson.gate.rank: That one is for a higher rank. Sail at your own for now.
sail.lesson.gate.weather: No going afloat today: look at the mast by the boathouse, it explains everything.
sail.lesson.gybing.done: Clean. Everyone's afraid of the gybe until they've done one, and now you have.
sail.lesson.gybing.fail: Ashore. Dry off, have some tea and we'll try again — the gybe comes on the third go.
sail.lesson.gybing.hint1: Gather the sheet before you turn and hand the boom across! Keep her flat, don't let her round up.
sail.lesson.gybing.hint2: Leave the buoys on opposite sides: gybe at the far one, tack at the near one.
sail.lesson.gybing.intro: A tack turns the bow through the wind, a gybe turns the stern. The boom crosses the whole boat in one go, so: gather the sheet, tell yourself “gybe-oh!”, duck, cross over. Then two figure-eights round the buoys — a tack at one, a gybe at the other.
sail.lesson.gybing.title: Gybing and figure-eights
sail.lesson.irons.done: Sitting at the buoy as if she were tied to it. Plenty of people can make a boat go; the ones who can make it stop are helmsmen.
sail.lesson.irons.fail: That's all for today. Stopping is a delicate thing; we'll come back to it in a steadier wind.
sail.lesson.irons.hint1: Bow into the wind and push the boom away from you! Going astern the rudder works the other way round — don't argue with it.
sail.lesson.irons.hint2: Come at the buoy from below, from leeward, and two lengths off let the sheet go. She'll carry her way and stop on her own.
sail.lesson.irons.intro: A boat has no brake, but it has the wind. Point the bow into it and the sail flaps and you stop: you're head to wind. Push the boom out by hand and she'll go backwards. Today: three seconds of sternway, and a stop by the buoy.
sail.lesson.irons.obj2: Stop by the buoy: {0} of {1} s
sail.lesson.irons.title: Head to wind, sternway, stopping
sail.lesson.landing.done: Boat on the sand, paint still on, and you're dry. Go and see the head coach: I'd say it's time you had your certificate.
sail.lesson.landing.fail: Just bring her in, any way you can. We'll polish the pretty landing another day.
sail.lesson.landing.hint1: Leave the mark to port and don't hug it: half a length of water, then round.
sail.lesson.landing.hint2: Let the sheet go sooner than seems right. Board up! You walk in to a slip, you don't run.
sail.lesson.landing.intro: The last lesson before your certificate. One lap of the small triangle, marks to port, then in to the slip — quietly, as you'd come up to a sleeping cat. Lift the centreboard early; you won't need it in the shallows.
sail.lesson.landing.obj1: A lap of the small triangle: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.landing.obj2: Land at the slip at low speed: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.landing.title: The triangle and landing at the slip
sail.lesson.mob.done: Both times you came up so sweetly the buoy could have climbed in by itself. I hope you never need this. But you have it now.
sail.lesson.mob.fail: Back we go. The buoy will wait; he's the patient sort.
sail.lesson.mob.hint1: Don't lose sight of him! Approach from leeward and three lengths off dump the sheet — she should drift up on her own.
sail.lesson.mob.intro: This buoy is your crewmate, and he's gone over the side. He won't sink, but he's cold and rather hurt about it. Reach away, tack, come back to him from leeward and stop alongside. Slowly. You don't pick up a friend at full speed.
sail.lesson.mob.obj1: Pick up the buoy at low speed: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.mob.title: Man overboard
sail.lesson.points.done: All four. Now when somebody says “go on a broad reach” you won't be looking it up.
sail.lesson.points.fail: Back we go. The points of sail won't drift off — the wind draws them fresh every day.
sail.lesson.points.hint1: Close-hauled: sheet nearly all the way in, and you sit up on the windward side.
sail.lesson.points.hint2: Beam reach: ease the sheet halfway. The pennant at the masthead points straight across the boat.
sail.lesson.points.hint3: Broad reach: ease more, the boom goes out towards the shroud. Feel her take off?
sail.lesson.points.hint4: Run: sheet right out, centreboard half up. Watch the boom and don't let it fly across.
sail.lesson.points.intro: The wind has four doors. Close-hauled — hard against it. Beam reach — wind on your side. Broad reach — over your shoulder, the merriest one. A run — straight at your back. Sail half a minute on each and listen to how the boat changes.
sail.lesson.points.title: Points of sail
sail.lesson.racing.done: On the line on time and a clean lap. There's racing on Wednesday evening — come along, there's room on the line.
sail.lesson.racing.fail: We'll pack it in. People spend years learning to start, so we've all the time in the world.
sail.lesson.racing.hint1: Count out loud! At twenty seconds be three lengths below the line and getting up speed.
sail.lesson.racing.hint2: Up the beat, tack on tack. Windward mark to port, then down on a run — and remember the centreboard.
sail.lesson.racing.intro: A race is the same tacks and gybes, only with somebody alongside who badly wants to be first. Three minutes to go — the class flag. One minute — flag P. The horn — off you go. Your job: cross the line not before the horn and not more than five seconds after. Then a lap: up to the windward mark and back.
sail.lesson.racing.obj1: Start within 5 seconds of the horn: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.racing.title: The start and a first lap
sail.lesson.shore.done: The knots hold, the boat's together and there's nothing left over. From this minute you're a deckhand. Tomorrow — afloat.
sail.lesson.shore.fail: That'll do for today. The knots won't go anywhere overnight — we'll finish another time.
sail.lesson.shore.hint1: The knot board's in the classroom, on the wall by the door. Bowline, figure-eight, reef knot: everyone starts with those.
sail.lesson.shore.hint2: The demonstration boat's on its trolley by the flag mast. Walk her from bow to rudder.
sail.lesson.shore.hint3: Your Luch is in the park, number nine. Mast, boom, sheet, rudder — in that order and nothing goes wrong.
sail.lesson.shore.intro: The sea can wait. Hands first: three knots at the board, then show me what's what on the boat, then rig her yourself. No hurry — a boat doesn't care for people in a rush.
sail.lesson.shore.obj1: Tie knots at the board: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.shore.obj2: Go over the demonstration boat: {0} of {1}
sail.lesson.shore.title: Ashore: knots, the boat, rigging
sail.lesson.tacking.done: Five tacks and never once stuck head to wind. Now you can get to any point on the sea. Even the one the wind comes from.
sail.lesson.tacking.fail: Home we go. Tacking is habit, and nobody builds a habit in a day.
sail.lesson.tacking.hint1: Sheet in and come up until the front edge of the sail shivers — then bear away a touch. That edge is where you live.
sail.lesson.tacking.hint2: Get her moving first, then tiller away — and mean it! Cross over, steady her. Never go into a tack without speed.
sail.lesson.tacking.intro: Nobody sails straight into the wind, not even me. You zigzag: close to the wind, tack, close again. Today we hold close-hauled and do five tacks. Duck on the tack — the boom doesn't stop to say hello.
sail.lesson.tacking.title: Close-hauled and tacking

sail.tutor.board_up: Board up! You don't come ashore with the centreboard down.
sail.tutor.calm: Flat calm. Sit forward, leave the tiller alone and wait — the wind always comes back.
sail.tutor.capsize: Easy! Hold on to the boat. Swim round to the centreboard, I'm right here.
sail.tutor.good_start: Good start! Now don't look back — sail the boat.
sail.tutor.gust: Gust coming — see the dark water? Ease the sheet and hike out!
sail.tutor.irons: You're in irons! Tiller hard over, push the boom out — the bow falls off and away you go.
sail.tutor.missed_mark: You've missed a mark! Go back; the lap doesn't count without it.
sail.tutor.ocs: Over early! Come back wholly behind the line and start again.
sail.tutor.outside: You're too far out! Turn back towards the buoys; it's deeper there and I'm closer.
sail.tutor.penalty_done: Turn done. Sail on; there's still everything to win back.
sail.tutor.recall: Everybody in! Three blasts isn't a request. Follow the launch.
sail.tutor.reef: It's freshening. We go reefed today: less sail, a calmer head.
sail.tutor.righted: She's up! Climb in over the stern, bail her out and get your breath.
sail.tutor.shallow: Shallow! Centreboard half up before it touches.
sail.tutor.touch: You touched the mark! Get clear and do one full turn — then carry on.
sail.tutor.well_done: That's it! Let your hands remember how that felt.
sail.tutor.wrong_side: Wrong side! The mark goes to port. Go back and round it properly.
